\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=multi, subtopic={Viscosity}, answer={B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S3 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: viscous shear stress, flow between coaxial cylinders | steps: stress tau = eta dv/dr; r*tau constant so v(r) is logarithmic; apply the two boundary conditions; force per unit length at the inner cylinder; radius where v = 0; check options | I: r*tau = const}]

\bfig{135.6}{SI12_p1_phy_s1_q04_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Force per unit length required to keep the inner cylinder moving is $4\pi\eta v_0$}
\opt{B}{Force per unit length required to keep the inner cylinder moving is $\dfrac{6\pi\eta v_0}{\ell n2}$}
\opt{C}{Distance of the point from the axis at which speed of fluid is zero is $2^{1/3}R$}
\opt{D}{Distance of the point from the axis at which speed of fluid is zero is $\sqrt2\,R$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P2-PHY-S2-Q01, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=2, qno=1, type=numerical, subtopic={Surface tension}, answer={1.50}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S3 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: surface tension force on a soap film, equilibrium | steps: geometry of the film between the squares; vertical component of tension per side; total upward force; weight of the small square; solve for h | I: the film tilts so only a component supports the weight}]
Figure shows a soap film formed between two square figures made of a uniform wire. The bigger square is held while keeping it in a horizontal plane and the smaller square is slowly allowed to drop vertically. It reaches an equilibrium state after dropping a height $h$. Let surface tension of soap $=T$. Mass per unit length of wire $=\lambda$. Acceleration due to gravity $=g$. Given that $h=\dfrac{n\lambda ga}{\sqrt{4T^2-\lambda^2g^2}}$; find the value $n$.
\bfig{158.2}{SI12_p2_phy_s2_q01_1.png}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P2-PHY-S2-Q02, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Viscosity}, answer={2.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: terminal velocity in a viscous fluid | steps: mg = buoyancy + 6 pi eta r v, with rho = 2 rho\_L gives v = 2 cm/s}]
A spherical ball of density $\rho$ and radius 0.003 m is dropped into a tube containing a viscous fluid. Viscosity of the fluid $=1.260$ N.m$^{-2}$ and its density $\rho_L=\rho/2=1260$ kg.m$^{-3}$. Find its terminal speed in cm/s. ($g=$ acceleration due to gravity $=10$ ms$^{-2}$)
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA01-P1-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Score Advanced - Test 01 (22 Sep 2020)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Pressure}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: hemisphere filled through a tube, pressure | steps: pressure of the liquid; force on the hemisphere; condition for lifting}]
A hollow thin hemisphere of mass M and radius R lies on a flat horizontal rubber surface. In the upper hemisphere there is a small hole in which a long thin tube is inserted (Fig.). Hemisphere tube is filled with water. To what maximum height can be poured the water into the tube?\par
\bfig{81.4}{SA01_p1_phy_s1_q03_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{M}{\pi R^2\rho}+\dfrac23R$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{M}{\pi R^2\rho}+\dfrac13R$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{M}{2\pi R^2\rho}+\dfrac23R$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{M}{\pi R^2\rho}+\dfrac43R$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA01-P2-PHY-S3-Q04, source={Score Advanced - Test 01 (22 Sep 2020)}, paper=2, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Surface tension}, answer={3.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: rubber loop on a liquid film, surface tension | steps: surface tension force; tension of the band; modulus relation}]
A very thin loop of rubber band of length $\ell=\dfrac{\pi R}2$ and cross-section A$_\perp$ is placed on a film of the liquid. The liquid dilates it to a circle of radius R after the film has been punctured inside the loop. Assume that Hooke's law holds for the rubber and that Young's modulus for rubber is Y. If the surface tension of the liquid is $\mathrm N\dfrac{\mathrm{YA}_\perp}{\mathrm R}$, find N.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA06-P2-PHY-S1-Q01, source={Score Advanced - Test 06 (04 Sep 2021)}, paper=2, qno=1, type=multi, subtopic={Viscosity}, answer={A,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: draining of one tank into another through a narrow tube, viscosity, Poiseuille flow gives exponential decay of the level difference | steps: Poiseuille flow gives exponential decay of the level difference}]
Two identical cylindrical tanks are connected by a narrow tube with a cork at its middle (fig). The radius of a tank is R = 20.0 cm, the radius of the tube is r = 1.0 mm. The length of the tube is $\ell$ = 1m. Water ($\rho$ = 1000 kg/m$^3$) is poured into one of the tanks to a height of h = 50 cm, while the second tank is empty. At the instant t = 0, the cork is opened. [Both the tanks are open at top]\par
\bfig{63.9}{SA06_p2_phy_s1_q01_1.png}
(viscosity of water $\eta$ = 1$\times$10$^{-3}$ Pa-s)\par
Given poiseuelle eqn for volume flow rate of fluid in a tube\par
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\Delta P\,\pi r^4}{8\eta L}$\par
$\Delta$P $\rightarrow$ pressure difference across ends of the tube\par
r $\rightarrow$ radius of tube\par
L $\rightarrow$ length of tube
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The difference between the levels of the water in the tanks decreases e times in time 1.6 $\times$ 10$^4$ s}
\opt{B}{The difference between the levels of the water in the tanks decreases e times in time 3.2 $\times$ 10$^4$ s}
\opt{C}{Total mechanical energy of the fluid is conserved during the process}
\opt{D}{Water level in the two containers cannot become equal in a finite time}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
